newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Ukraine agree to end Black Sea fleet row.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Ukraine agree to end Black Sea fleet row.

text.p: Russian leader Boris Yeltsin and Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma on Thursday resolved all the problems surrounding a protracted dispute over dividing the Black Sea fleet, a Yeltsin spokesman said.

Sergei Yastrzhembsky said they agreed to end the row, which has dragged on since the Soviet Union fell apart in 1991, at a 30-minute meeting in the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow where Yeltsin is preparing for heart surgery.
Several such deals have been announced in the past but the fate of the 600-ship fleet has not yet been settled and the problem is a continuing irritant for both countries.
Just before the two leaders met, Russia's lower house of parliament warned Ukraine that Moscow would never hand over control of the Crimean port of Sevastopol, home to the fleet.
But the State Duma's resolution -- passed a day after Russian deputies voted overwhelmingly to stop the fleet being divided up -- had no legal force.

"The presidents reached agreement on all the questions. Before the middle of November it is expected that Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will visit Kiev when a number of agreements will be signed on splitting up the fleet, where it will be based and on financing as well," Yastrzhembsky said.
But he hinted at possible trouble to come by saying the question of Sevastopol's status had been removed from the agenda, rather than confirming the matter had been solved.

Yeltsin promised Kuchma that his first official visit after he had recovered from heart surgery planned for next month would be to Kiev to sign a long-awaited agreement on relations betwen the two major Slav states.
Before Yeltsin fell ill in June, he postponed six trips to Kiev in 20 months to sign a planned friendship treaty in a clear signal that Moscow was not happy with the state of relations.
The dispute over the ageing Black Sea fleet has defied all previous attempts to solve it.

Broad accords have already been signed dividing the fleet but no decision has been reached on a share-out of bases and the future of Sevastopol, which the Duma said still fell under Russian jurisdiction although Crimea is part of Ukraine.

"Sevastopol was, is and will be the main naval base of Russia's Black Sea fleet. Unilateral moves by Ukraine to divide it will lead not just to the division but the destruction of the Black Sea fleet -- the Duma thinks the division of the fleet has to be stopped," said Thursday's appeal.

The Duma said a Soviet decree of 1948 which put Sevastopol under Moscow's direct rule was still valid and that Russia, as the successor state to the Soviet Union, therefore had jurisdiction over the port.
Deputies say the fleet, created more than 200 years ago, would not survive the split and would leave both Russia and Ukraine without a Black Sea naval force.
Kuchma reacted angrily to Wednesday's vote, saying it could lead to "a worsening in relations between the Ukrainian and Russian people" and not just between two legislatures.
But in an indication that Kiev could be softening its position, three senior Ukrainian navy officials who oppose giving in to Russia on the issue resigned on Thursday.
